notice: Ground truth for a synthetic case. The evidence describes a fictional meal-kit subscription business. No real Walmart data is used and no access to any Walmart system is claimed.
authoring_limitation: Authored by the same person who wrote the corpus. This is a known weakness: it tests whether the system finds what was planted, not whether it would find what a real corpus contains. Recorded in docs/04-evaluation.md rather than hidden.
question: Which intervention should the team prioritise to reduce subscriber churn?
desired_outcome: Reduce subscriber churn, and in particular retain more new subscribers past their first month, without raising cost per retained subscriber or creating unacceptable subscriber, operational, or governance risk.

scoring_rules.recall_denominator: Only entries with must_detect true count toward recall. GT-M6 is must_detect false: it is a real gap, but finding it is credit rather than a requirement. Hazards GT-H2 and GT-H3 are likewise recorded rather than required; GT-H1 is required, because the corpus states both halves of it explicitly and only the consequence has to be joined up.
scoring_rules.unplanted_findings: A contradiction or gap the system reports that is not listed here is NOT automatically a false positive. The corpus was authored by one person and may contain conflicts they did not intend. Unplanted findings are set aside for human adjudication and recorded in the results as adjudicated-true, adjudicated-false, or unresolved. Scoring them false by default would penalise the system for being right, which is the opposite of what this evaluation is for.
scoring_rules.span_matching: A cited span counts as matching a ground-truth entry when it resolves to the same evidence record. Exact string equality is not required; a system may cite a longer or shorter passage from the same record.
scoring_rules.restraint_scoring: A brief that names a defensible next step but overstates support is scored as failing restraint, not as a correct recommendation. Naming the right option is necessary but not sufficient.
scoring_rules.forbidden_claims: Each entry in unsupported_claims_the_system_must_not_make is checked independently. Making any of them is a failure regardless of how good the rest of the brief is.

expected_contradictions.topic: what actually causes subscribers to cancel

side_a.span: Recipe variety is the dominant reason subscribers give for leaving.

expected_contradictions.why_it_matters: 62.4% of cancellations happen within 21 days, when a subscriber has received at most three boxes and the first two came from a fixed six-recipe starter menu that sits outside the rotation. Recipe variety is the leading stated reason and cannot be what the majority of leavers experienced. Neither side is wrong: the survey records what a real group of people said, and the tenure distribution records what a larger group did. A brief that picks one side targets the wrong cohort, and a brief that averages them targets nobody.
expected_contradictions.how_to_resolve: Cross-tabulate the exit-survey reason against tenure at cancellation. Both fields are already in the survey export and have never been joined. If variety complaints come almost entirely from respondents past day 60, the two findings are true of different cohorts and imply different interventions. If variety complaints are spread evenly across tenure, respondents are naming a reason they could not have experienced and the survey is measuring narrative rather than cause.

side_a.span: Monthly churn improved to 6.9% in Q1 after two quarters of increase

side_b.span: note: definition changed on 2026-01-01 - paused subscribers are no longer counted as cancellations - synthetic

expected_contradictions.why_it_matters: The Q1 improvement coincides exactly with a definition change that moved paused subscribers out of the numerator. Pausing rose from 1.1% to 2.9% per month in the same quarter, and 61.0% of subscribers who paused cancelled within 90 days. The improvement may be entirely definitional, and the FY26 target is being tracked against a series that changed mid-flight.
expected_contradictions.how_to_resolve: Restate 2026-Q1 and 2026-Q2 monthly churn under the pre-2026 definition by adding paused subscribers back into the numerator. Every input exists in the corpus: pause_rate from 2025-Q4 onward, pause_to_cancellation_within_90_days, and the active-subscriber base. One recomputed series settles whether churn improved or only the definition did.

expected_contradictions.topic: whether delivery reliability is a problem

side_a.span: Network on-time delivery was 96.2% in 2026-Q2, comfortably above the 95% service standard.

expected_contradictions.why_it_matters: The network figure averages three sites that do not serve the same subscribers. New subscribers are routed to Ashby by default, and Ashby handled 71% of first boxes in the quarter while running 7.5 points below the network figure and 6.3 points below the service standard. The cohort where churn concentrates is being described by a number computed mostly over everybody else.
expected_contradictions.how_to_resolve: Report on-time delivery and box completeness for first boxes specifically, split by site. The routing rule and the per-site rates are both already recorded; the first-box rate has simply never been computed as its own number. If first-box on-time is near 88.7%, the two statements are consistent and the network average is the misleading one.

expected_contradictions.topic: whether food waste still argues against a wider menu

side_a.span: food waste ran at 9.4% of ingredient cost under forecast-to-order sourcing

side_b.span: Waste has run at 4.1% of ingredient cost since the committed-volume sourcing agreement began in February 2026.

expected_contradictions.why_it_matters: The menu was cut from 20 recipes to 14 because waste was running at 9.4%. Sourcing changed in February 2026 and waste has more than halved. A brief that treats the October 2025 decision as a standing objection to menu breadth is citing a rationale the corpus has already overtaken.
expected_contradictions.how_to_resolve: The waste rationale is superseded and should not be quoted as a live objection. The remaining objection is capacity, not cost: Ashby cannot support more than 18 weekly recipes before a second pick line is commissioned in Q1 2027. That bounds any menu expansion at 18, independently of waste.

expected_missing_evidence.why_it_matters: This is the single join that would reconcile the qualitative and behavioural evidence. Without it the corpus supports two incompatible readings of the same problem and cannot choose between them.
expected_missing_evidence.how_to_obtain: Cross-tabulate the existing survey export: reason category by tenure-at-cancellation band. No new collection is required.

expected_missing_evidence.question: Why do payment-lapse cancellations happen, and how many recover without intervention?
expected_missing_evidence.why_it_matters: Payment lapse is the largest cancellation channel at 47.2% and the corpus contains no evidence of any kind about it: no reasons, no recovery rate, no test, no instrumentation. The largest single group of leavers is entirely unexplained.
expected_missing_evidence.how_to_obtain: Instrument the payment-failure path, then measure the 30-day self-recovery rate and the decline-reason mix from the billing processor before designing any intervention.

expected_missing_evidence.question: What is monthly churn on a single consistent definition across 2025 and 2026?
expected_missing_evidence.why_it_matters: The series changed definition on 2026-01-01. Every trend statement in the corpus, including the objectives document and the growth lead's claim that churn turned the corner, rests on comparing figures computed two different ways.
expected_missing_evidence.how_to_obtain: Restate 2026-Q1 and 2026-Q2 with paused subscribers added back into the numerator, and publish both series side by side.

anchor.span: from 2026-01-01, subscribers who pause are reported as active rather than as cancellations

expected_missing_evidence.question: What is on-time delivery and box completeness for first boxes specifically?
expected_missing_evidence.why_it_matters: First boxes are routed disproportionately to the worst-performing site and show item substitution at 9.6% against 3.9% for later boxes, but no first-box service figure exists. The strongest behavioural lead in the corpus is measured only indirectly.
expected_missing_evidence.how_to_obtain: Split the existing on-time and completeness measures by box sequence number and by site.

anchor.span: First-box performance has never been reported separately from the network figure.

expected_missing_evidence.question: Does menu breadth affect subscribers in their first 30 days?
expected_missing_evidence.why_it_matters: The only expanded-menu test excluded first-30-day subscribers by design, which is precisely the cohort where cancellations concentrate. The null result does not apply to them, and no other evidence does either.
expected_missing_evidence.how_to_obtain: Re-run the expanded-menu test with early-tenure subscribers included, or vary the starter menu rather than the rotation.

anchor.span: The pilot excluded subscribers in their first 30 days by design

expected_missing_evidence.question: How many cancelled subscribers come back on their own?
expected_missing_evidence.why_it_matters: The reactivation metric exists in the table but was never populated. A blank is not a zero, and a material self-reactivation rate would change how much any win-back or recovery intervention is worth.
expected_missing_evidence.how_to_obtain: Populate reactivation_rate_within_180_days, noting that the 180-day record-minimisation policy bounds how far back it can be computed.

evidence_hazards.description: The exit survey is a page in the account-page cancellation flow and has no email, SMS or telephone equivalent. It is therefore offered only to the 34.1% of cancellations that go through that flow, and never to the 47.2% closed on payment failure or the 18.7% closed by an agent. The corpus never states this consequence; it is recoverable only by reading the survey-tooling note against the channel breakdown.
evidence_hazards.why_it_matters: Every qualitative finding in the case is drawn from a minority of leavers, selected by their willingness and ability to log in and complete a cancellation flow. That is not a random third. It skews toward engaged, longer-tenure subscribers and away from anyone whose relationship ended because a card stopped working or whose box never arrived, which is exactly why the survey shows delivery complaints at 8.4% while the behavioural data shows first-delivery problems at 11.4% among the fastest churners. This hazard is what tempts GT-U1, GT-U4 and GT-U7.

evidence_hazards.hazard: averaged rate hiding a split across populations
evidence_hazards.span: Network on-time delivery was 96.2% in 2026-Q2, comfortably above the 95% service standard.
evidence_hazards.description: The network on-time figure averages a mature site at 97.9% with a ramping site at 88.7%. The two sites do not serve the same subscribers: new subscribers are routed to the weaker one by default.
evidence_hazards.why_it_matters: The average is used in the report to declare delivery above standard. For the cohort that actually churns, it is roughly seven and a half points optimistic.

evidence_hazards.span: note: definition changed on 2026-01-01 - paused subscribers are no longer counted as cancellations - synthetic

evidence_hazards.why_it_matters: The apparent Q4-to-Q1 improvement is the first point after the change. Any trend read across the boundary is comparing two different measures.

unsupported_claims_the_system_must_not_m.claim: Recipe variety is the main reason subscribers cancel.
unsupported_claims_the_system_must_not_m.why_forbidden: It is the main reason given by 89 people drawn from one of three cancellation paths, covering at most 34.1% of leavers. 62.4% of cancellations happen before a third box, and the first two boxes are a fixed starter menu outside the rotation. The claim is defensible only with both a channel and a tenure qualifier.

recommendation_restraint.reason: The two strongest signals in the corpus describe different populations and neither is wrong. The qualitative evidence is collected on one of three cancellation paths and cannot speak for the 65.9% of leavers on the other two. The behavioural evidence locates churn in the first 21 days but has never been joined to any reason data. The largest cancellation channel has no evidence of any kind attached to it, and the churn series changed definition mid-flight. No option can be supported more than moderately on this evidence, and a brief that resolves the qualitative-quantitative conflict by choosing a side, or by averaging the two, has overstated what the corpus establishes.
defensible_next_steps: Cross-tabulate exit-survey reason against tenure at cancellation and against channel. It requires no new collection and is the single analysis that would separate the two competing readings.
Compute first-box on-time and completeness by site, and act on the routing of new subscribers to the ramping site if the gap holds.
Instrument the payment-failure path so the largest cancellation channel stops being invisible, before designing any recovery intervention for it.
Restate monthly churn on one definition before any target or trend claim is made.

must_not_recommend_without_conditions.why: Supported only by executive preference and a vendor claim with no method. Its best signal is special-category data barred from marketing use, every generated line requires human review, and a new processor needs a five-to-seven-week assessment.

Menu expansion is supported by stated reasons from a channel-restricted survey and contradicted by the only randomised test. It is also capped at 18 weekly recipes until a second pick line is commissioned in Q1 2027.
Win-back cannot reach the payment-lapse channel at all, because no cancellation event is emitted there, and requires a separate retention-contact consent of unquantified coverage.

restraint_signals_that_must_appear: The brief must state that the survey evidence and the tenure evidence describe different populations, and must not resolve the conflict by choosing one side or by averaging them.
The brief must say what would settle the conflict: joining exit-survey reason to tenure at cancellation.
The brief must qualify any exit-survey finding by the cancellation channel it was collected on, and must not present it as representative of cancellations overall.
The brief must not present the Q1 churn improvement as real without flagging the 2026-01-01 definition change.
The brief must not present executive or culinary preference as evidence.
